lessons.title: Getting to know the poultry farm
lessons.html:
Getting to know the poultry farm

A poultry farm is a busy place with many birds in houses. Every worker has a job that keeps the birds healthy and safe.

Parts of the farm

  • The gate and fence keep out people, animals and vehicles that are not allowed in.
  • The change room and showers: you change into clean farm clothes and boots before you go to the houses.
  • The poultry houses: long buildings where the birds live. They have feeders, drinkers, fans, lights and heaters.
  • The feed silos outside each house hold the feed.
  • The egg room on a layer farm, where eggs are collected, cleaned and packed.
  • The store for tools, medicines and cleaning products.
  • The generator gives power when the electricity goes off.
  • The dead bird area, where dead birds are put for safe disposal.

Types of birds

Broilers are chickens grown for meat. They grow very fast. Layers are hens that lay eggs. Breeders are hens and roosters whose eggs hatch into chicks.

People on the farm

The farm manager runs the farm. The supervisor plans the work and checks it. General workers feed and water birds, clean houses, collect eggs and remove dead birds. A vet visits to check the birds' health.

Your daily work

Your work may include checking feed and water, walking the house to look at the birds, picking up dead birds, collecting eggs, cleaning, and writing numbers on the house record card. Always tell your supervisor when something is wrong.

lessons.title: Biosecurity and hygiene rules
lessons.html:
Biosecurity and hygiene rules

Biosecurity means keeping germs away from the birds. Chickens live close together. One sick bird can make the whole house sick. Some diseases, like bird flu (avian influenza), can kill many birds very fast.

Rules you must follow

  1. Only go onto the farm through the main gate.
  2. Shower or wash and change into clean farm clothes and boots every time you come in.
  3. Use the foot bath at the door of each house. Step in with both boots.
  4. Wash or sanitise your hands before you go into a house.
  5. Do not keep your own chickens, ducks or birds at home if the farm says you may not.
  6. Do not bring food, chicken or eggs from outside into the houses.
  7. Do not go from one house to another without following the farm's rules. Usually you work in young birds first, then older birds.
  8. Keep doors closed so wild birds and rats cannot get in.

Visitors

Visitors must sign the visitor book and follow the same rules. Do not let anyone into a house without permission.

Keeping clean

  • Wash your hands after the toilet, after touching dead birds and before eating.
  • Eat only in the place set out for eating.
  • Keep the area around the houses clean and free of feed spills, so rats do not come.

Why it matters

If disease comes onto the farm, many birds may die or be killed. The farm loses money and workers may lose jobs. Following the rules keeps the birds, the farm and your job safe.

lessons.title: Working safely on a poultry farm
lessons.html:
Working safely on a poultry farm

Dangers on a poultry farm

DangerHow to stay safe
Dust and ammonia smellWear the dust mask the farm gives you. Report a strong ammonia smell.
Cleaning chemicals and disinfectantsWear gloves, goggles and boots. Read the label. Never mix chemicals.
ElectricityDo not touch wires, plugs or panels with wet hands. Report damaged cables.
Fans and moving partsKeep hands and clothes away. Never remove guards.
LiftingBend your knees, keep your back straight, get help with heavy bags.
Slippery floorsWear boots with grip. Clean up spills.
Heat in summerDrink water often. Take breaks.

Germs from birds

Some germs from birds and manure can make people sick, like Salmonella. Always wash your hands. If you get sick with fever or flu signs after working with sick birds, tell your supervisor and go to the clinic.

Fire

Know where the fire extinguishers are. Do not smoke near houses, feed or the generator. If there is a fire, shout to warn others, get out and call your supervisor.

Injuries

Report every injury, even a small cut. The OHS Act 85 of 1993 says the employer must keep the workplace safe and workers must work safely and report dangers. Use the first aid box and tell your supervisor.

Treat birds kindly

Handle birds gently. Do not kick, throw or hit them. The Animals Protection Act 71 of 1962 makes cruelty to animals against the law.

Key points

  • A poultry farm has houses, silos, a change room, an egg room and a generator.
  • Shower, change clothes and use the foot bath before going into houses.
  • Keep doors closed to keep out wild birds and rats.
  • Wear your mask, gloves and boots and never mix chemicals.
  • Report every injury and handle birds gently.
